mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of falling unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in 2 months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over 3 months, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong labor market indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% signals inflationary pressure, which erodes real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of GDP (GDPC1) exceeds 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (growth < 2%), it signals strong real economic growth without significant inflationary pressure, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 3% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth < 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong GDP growth and stable inflation.
